messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1871678424000050
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nbt.2024.02.003

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: DNA ENTRAP (DNA ENhanced TRAnsfer Platform) - Droplet Microfluidic XPORT-Mediated Conjugation Between Bacillus subtilis Donor and Recipient Strains

REAGENTS USED:
  - B. subtilis Donor Strain JAB981 (XPORT donor derived from B. subtilis JH642, tetracycline-resistant, xylose-inducible conjugative machinery)
  - B. subtilis Recipient Strain JAB545 (derivative of B. subtilis PY79, chloramphenicol-resistant, comK-interrupted so unable to take up DNA by chemical/natural competence)
  - LB Media supplemented with 100 ug/mL D-alanine and 10 ug/mL tetracycline (donor culture medium)
  - LB Media, no supplementation (recipient culture medium)
  - Xylose Inducer (50% xylose solution, induces conjugative element production in the donor)
  - Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) wash buffer
  - Resuspension Media (fresh LB supplemented with 100 ug/mL D-alanine, used to normalize OD600 and set donor:recipient ratios)
  - Carrier Oil/Surfactant Phase (Novec 7500 fluorinated oil with 1.25 wt/wt% Pico-Surf 1 surfactant)
  - Selection Agars: LB agar (recipients + transconjugants), LB + 10 ug/mL tetracycline agar (transconjugants only), LB + 100 ug/mL D-alanine + 10 ug/mL tetracycline agar (donors + transconjugants)
  - IPTG Induction Reagent (1 mM, induces the miniICE-encoded GFPmut2 reporter in transconjugants)

STEPS:
1. Pick single colonies of donor (JAB981) and recipient (JAB545) strains and culture in selective LB media (donor: +D-alanine+tetracycline; recipient: no supplement) until OD600 > 1.2.
2. Sub-culture both strains into fresh media at a starting OD600 = 0.025 and incubate at 37 C, 225 rpm.
3. Grow the donor sub-culture for 1.5 h until OD600 = 0.15, then add 50% xylose (60 uL) to induce conjugative element production.
4. Continue culturing both donor and recipient for another 1.5 h until OD600 = 0.9-1.1.
5. Pellet 2.5 mL of each culture by centrifugation, wash twice with PBS (repeating the pellet/wash cycle), and resuspend in 500 uL sterile PBS.
6. Resuspend both strains in fresh LB media supplemented with 100 ug/mL D-alanine to a final OD600 = 0.6, at the desired donor:recipient ratio (3:1 or 1:1).
7. Inject the donor and recipient cell suspensions into the DNA ENTRAP microfluidic chip via two distinct cell-port inlets at equal flow rates, together with the fluorinated oil/surfactant carrier phase, to generate cell-encapsulated droplets of 60 um diameter (approximately 20-30 cells per droplet).
8. Flow the droplets into the downstream "first-in-first-out" micro-vessel incubation system and co-incubate for the designated period (0.5 h, 1 h, or 2 h) to allow XPORT-mediated conjugation to occur.
9. Remove ~50 uL of total droplet/carrier-oil volume from the incubator at each timepoint and spread 16 uL onto each of three selection agar plates: LB agar (recipients + transconjugants), LB+tetracycline agar (transconjugants only), and LB+D-alanine+tetracycline agar (donors + transconjugants); incubate plates at 37 C for 16 h.
10. Calculate conjugation efficiency (TC/D) by subtracting colony-forming-unit counts between the selective plates to isolate donor, recipient, and transconjugant populations.
11. Confirm successful conjugation by colony PCR amplification and whole-genome sequencing of the miniICE insertion site in transconjugant colonies (primers flanking the trnS-leu2 integration locus).
12. Pick transconjugant colonies, induce with 1 mM IPTG for 1 h, and quantify GFPmut2 reporter expression by flow cytometry to confirm functional miniICE cassette integration, compared against benchtop-generated transconjugants.

INTERPRETATION: Successful in-droplet XPORT-mediated conjugation is confirmed by colony growth specifically on the tetracycline-selective plates (transconjugants), a conjugation efficiency (TC/D ratio) that is 2-fold to over 20-fold higher for droplet-based conjugation compared to the benchtop approach (peak efficiency at the 1 h co-incubation timepoint for both 3:1 and 1:1 donor:recipient ratios), correct miniICE insertion at the trnS-leu2 locus confirmed by sequencing, and IPTG-induced GFPmut2 fluorescence intensities in droplet transconjugants that are statistically indistinguishable from benchtop transconjugants, along with donor and recipient cell viabilities remaining above 98% throughout the 12 h in-droplet incubation window.

ir.content:
bsbbif_2_t:
	dispose(tc_plate1[0])
bsbbif_3_f:
	PHI tc_plate2 = {tc_plate1,tc_plate}
main:
	donor1[0] = dispense(donor_cells)
	heat(donor1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 5400.0SECOND
	xylose1[0] = dispense(xylose_inducer)
	induced_donor1[0] = mix(donor1[0], xylose1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(induced_donor1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 5400.0SECOND
	recipient1[0] = dispense(recipient_cells)
	heat(recipient1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 5400.0SECOND
	wash11[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	washed_donor1[0] = mix(induced_donor1[0], wash11[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	wash21[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	washed_recipient1[0] = mix(recipient1[0], wash21[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	media11[0] = dispense(resuspension_media)
	resuspended_donor1[0] = mix(washed_donor1[0], media11[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	media21[0] = dispense(resuspension_media)
	resuspended_recipient1[0] = mix(washed_recipient1[0], media21[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	cell_mix1[0] = mix(resuspended_donor1[0], resuspended_recipient1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	oil1[0] = dispense(oil_surfactant)
	droplet1[0] = mix(cell_mix1[0], oil1[0]) @ 10.0SECOND
	heat(droplet1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 3600.0SECOND
	recipient_agar1[0] = dispense(lb_agar)
	recipient_plate1[0] = mix(droplet1[0], recipient_agar1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(recipient_plate1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND
	tc_agar1[0] = dispense(tet_agar)
	tc_plate1[0] = mix(droplet1[0], tc_agar1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(tc_plate1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND
	donor_agar1[0] = dispense(dalanine_tet_agar)
	donor_plate1[0] = mix(droplet1[0], donor_agar1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(donor_plate1[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND
	conjugation_signal1[0] = detect(fluorescence, tc_plate1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	if conjugation_signal1[0] < 50	|	true: jump bsbbif_2_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_3_f
bsbbr_4_h:
	PHI REPEAT_31 = {REPEAT_30,REPEAT_32}
	PHI gfp_signal1 = {gfp_signal0,gfp_signal2}
	PHI inducer1 = {inducer0,inducer2}
	PHI induced_colony1 = {induced_colony0,induced_colony3}
	PHI colony1 = {colony0,colony2}
	if REPEAT_31[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_5_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_8_f
bsbbr_5_t:
	colony2[0] = dispense(recipient_cells)
	inducer2[0] = dispense(iptg)
	induced_colony2[0] = mix(colony2[0], inducer2[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	heat(induced_colony2[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 3600.0SECOND
	gfp_signal2[0] = detect(fluorescence, induced_colony2[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	if gfp_signal2[0] < 50	|	true: jump bsbbif_6_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_7_f
bsbbif_6_t:
	dispose(induced_colony2[0])
bsbbif_7_f:
	PHI induced_colony3 = {induced_colony2,induced_colony}
	REPEAT_32[0] = REPEAT_31[0] - 1
	jump: bsbbr_4_h
bsbbr_8_f:
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.field: droplet co-incubation modeled only at 60m (1 h)
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper tested three co-incubation timepoints (0.5 h, 1 h, 2 h) across two donor:recipient ratios (3:1, 1:1). Only the 1 h timepoint, identified as the peak-conjugation-frequency point, is modeled here; the 0.5 h/2 h timepoints and the 3:1 ratio experiment are not separately represented.

BioScript has no primitive for two-inlet microfluidic co-flow, droplet pinch-off geometry, or flow-rate control. The 'droplet = mix cell_mix with oil' step stands in for the actual continuous droplet generator producing 60 um droplets at ~180-200 droplets/sec.

BioScript exposes only one generic detect module. It is reused for the qualitative tetracycline-plate colony/CFU screen (the paper's actual metric involves subtracting CFU counts across three plates, not a fluorescence signal) and for the literal GFPmut2 flow-cytometry fluorescence quantification.

These pass/fail cutoffs are illustrative placeholders; the paper reports specific conjugation efficiencies (e.g., ~3.5x10^-3 TC/D for droplet 1:1) and mean fluorescence intensities (e.g., 7828 +/- 629 for droplet transconjugants) rather than a stated binary detection threshold.

numeric_mismatches.field: droplet viability characterization, device fabrication, colony PCR/WGS confirmation, two-way ANOVA/Sidak statistics, CFU-subtraction efficiency calculation
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are downstream verification/statistical-analysis steps or one-time hardware-fabrication procedures with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and fall outside the scope of this translation.

metadata.notes: This protocol details DNA ENTRAP (DNA ENhanced TRAnsfer Platform) - Droplet Microfluidic XPORT-Mediated Conjugation Between Bacillus subtilis Donor and Recipient Strains. The assay is performed on a qPCR Thermocycler platform. Key reagents used in the assay include B. subtilis Donor Strain JAB981 and B. subtilis Recipient Strain JAB545.
